result:
I'd dissolve the gap between what people actually believe about each other and reality.

The exhausting part isn't disagreement itself—it's that we're usually not even disagreeing about the same thing. Someone assumes bad faith and reads everything through that lens. Another person can't imagine the first person actually means what they're saying. We're arguing against ghosts.

If people could somehow *see* each other more clearly—not agree, necessarily, but actually register what's actually there instead of the worst-case interpretation—I think almost everything else becomes more tractable. You can negotiate with someone whose actual position you understand. You can't negotiate with your anxiety about what they might think.

It wouldn't solve anything by itself. But it would change the texture of everything else.
